name: CA-50
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+10 district with a well-funded incumbent: Peters has $2.6M on hand and no outside spending against him
Challenger Steve Cohen reports no fundraising or outside support
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at about 96%
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: Peters holds a ten-point Democratic seat with a large cash advantage and zero outside opposition, while Cohen shows no measurable fundraising; markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent, supporting a Safe Democratic rating even with a slight shade below the fundamentals-only number given the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending, or a fundraising surge from Cohen would be the first sign the margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Scott Peters, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a San Diego-area district that leans about ten points Democratic. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $1.8 million and holding $2.6 million on hand, with no outside groups spending against him. Republican Steve Cohen reports no fundraising totals, leaving him with few visible resources for a competitive campaign.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96 percent. The combination of a favorable seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a lightly financed challenger points to a comfortable Democratic margin, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact size of the win.
